title: I Mean
subtitle: ဆိုလိုတာက…
review: Written by Claude. The Burmese lines are drafts: check every one before publishing or recording.

categories.my: ကိုယ့်စကားကို ပြန်ပြင်ခြင်း
categories.desc: Fixing what you just said: a wrong word, a wrong fact, or something that came out too strong.
cards: I mean…
ဆိုလိုတာက…
The quickest way to fix or sharpen what you just said. Very common in speech. Not: I am meaning.
It starts at six. I mean, at seven.
ခြောက်နာရီမှာ စမယ်။ ဆိုလိုတာက ခုနစ်နာရီမှာ။
Sorry, I meant Tuesday.
Meant (say ‘ment’) is the past of mean. Use it when you notice the mistake a moment later.
Did I say Monday? Sorry, I meant Tuesday.
Actually…
တကယ်တော့…
Gives the real fact, correcting yourself or the other person. Careful: actually does not mean ‘now’. For ‘now’, say currently or at the moment.
I saw him yesterday. Actually, it was two days ago.
မနေ့က သူ့ကို တွေ့တယ်။ တကယ်တော့ တမြန်နေ့ကပါ။
Or rather…
ပိုမှန်အောင် ပြောရရင်…
Swaps in a more exact word. A little careful. Common in writing too.
He's angry, or rather, disappointed.
သူ စိတ်ဆိုးနေတယ်၊ ပိုမှန်အောင် ပြောရရင် စိတ်ပျက်နေတာ။
Well, not exactly.
အင်း… အတိအကျတော့ မဟုတ်ဘူး။
Takes back part of what you said.
It's free. Well, not exactly. You pay for delivery.
အခမဲ့ပါ။ အင်း… အတိအကျတော့ မဟုတ်ဘူး။ ပို့ခတော့ ပေးရတယ်။

categories.desc: Saying the same thing again, more clearly or more simply.
cards: In other words…
တစ်နည်းအားဖြင့်…
Says it again in plainer words. Often it gives the conclusion the other person has not said out loud.
He never answers my messages. In other words, he isn't interested.
သူ ကျွန်မ မက်ဆေ့ချ်တွေကို ဘယ်တော့မှ ပြန်မဖြေဘူး။ တစ်နည်းအားဖြင့် စိတ်မဝင်စားဘူးပေါ့။
What I mean is…
Steps back to make your point clearly, often after someone has misunderstood you.
What I mean is, we should wait a little.
ကျွန်တော် ဆိုလိုတာက နည်းနည်း စောင့်သင့်တယ်။
That is…
Adds the exact meaning. Rather formal. In writing you will see i.e., which means the same.
She works from home, that is, she never goes to the office.
သူ အိမ်ကနေ အလုပ်လုပ်တယ်၊ ဆိုလိုတာကတော့ ရုံးကို ဘယ်တော့မှ မသွားဘူး။
Meaning?
A one-word question that asks the other person to explain. Let your voice go up. Friendly, but it can sound like a challenge.
— I've made a decision. — Meaning?
Let me put it another way.
For when your first explanation did not work. Put here means say.
Let me put it another way. We have no money left.

categories.desc: Buying time, or softening something that is hard to say.
cards: How can I put it…
ဘယ်လိုပြောရမလဲ…
A pause while you look for the right words, often before something delicate. Also: How shall I put this?
He's… how can I put it… not very careful.
သူက… ဘယ်လိုပြောရမလဲ… သိပ်ဂရုမစိုက်တတ်ဘူး။
I don't know how to say this.
ဒါကို ဘယ်လိုပြောရမှန်း မသိဘူး။
Said before bad news, or before something personal.
I don't know how to say this, but I lost your book.
ဘယ်လိုပြောရမှန်း မသိဘူး၊ ဒါပေမဲ့ မင်းစာအုပ် ပျောက်သွားတယ်။
Let's say…
Softens an answer when the plain one would be too blunt. Also: Let's just say…
— Did you like the food? — Let's say I wasn't very hungry.
Sort of.
Says a word is only roughly right. On its own, a careful yes. Also Kind of. In fast speech: sorta, kinda.
— Is he your boss? — Sort of. He's my team leader.

categories.desc: Small spoken words that fill a pause, or take the edge off what you just said.
cards: Like…
A very informal filler for an example or a rough idea. Young people use it a lot. Do not use it in writing or in exams.
It was, like, two hours late.
နှစ်နာရီလောက်ကို နောက်ကျတာ။
Well…
အင်း…
The pause before an answer, often an awkward one. Also Um… and Er…
Well… I'm not sure.
အင်း… မသေချာဘူး။
Mind you…
ဒါပေမဲ့လည်း…
Adds a ‘but’ to what you just said. British English. Americans say Then again…
It's expensive. Mind you, the quality is good.
ဈေးကြီးတယ်။ ဒါပေမဲ့လည်း အရည်အသွေးတော့ ကောင်းတယ်။
That said…
Balances what came before with a point on the other side. Also: Having said that…
He's often late. That said, he works hard.
သူ ခဏခဏ နောက်ကျတယ်။ ဒါပေမဲ့ အလုပ်တော့ ကြိုးစားတယ်။

categories.my: နားလည်ရဲ့လား စစ်ခြင်း
categories.desc: Making sure the listener is still with you.
cards: You know…
သိတယ်မလား…
Checks that the listener is following, or fills a pause. Used too often, it sounds unsure.
It's, you know, a bit difficult.
နည်းနည်း ခက်တယ်လေ၊ သိတယ်မလား။
You know what I mean?
ဘာပြောချင်လဲ သိတယ်မလား။
Asks whether your point got across, or the thing you did not say out loud.
He's nice, but… you know what I mean?
သူက သဘောကောင်းပါတယ်၊ ဒါပေမဲ့… ဘာပြောချင်လဲ သိတယ်မလား။
Does that make sense?
A polite check after an explanation. Kinder than Do you understand?, which can sound like a strict teacher.
Turn left, then right at the bank. Does that make sense?
